performances.jam: The second extended, highly improvisational "Free." An absolute tour-de-force, few Phish jams are as raw and intense as the Landover Free: almost uncomfortably so. Arising from rancor between Trey and Fish following a botched introduction to “Rift,” this multi-sectioned jam explores emotions of anger, contempt, release, and ultimately reconciliation over its 30+ minute voyage -- with Trey making three excursions to his mini-kit to spar with Fish (most notoriously when the rest of the band is ready to play “Bouncing” and Trey says no). Absurdly must-hear. Also includes "No Quarter" teases and a "BATR" tease. -> to "Llama."

performances.jam: The new or modern "Free" jam is hatched with funky, bass-led sound. Great Page on clavinet, organ, synthesizer and piano.
Nice funky jam that gets pretty rocking. Great Mike and Trey.
More of the modern "Free" jam, with a great bass-led breakdown and some good delay/resume action.
Slow tempo, very funky jam with Trey taking the lead.

After an amazing start to the II, it becomes clear that Trey has little interest in the "Hood" he dialed up following a great "Bowie." Check out the show for more details, but in lieu of "thanking" Mr. Minor, Trey aborts the song and ->'s into "Free". The band unleashes, resulting in one of the finest performances since 95. The jam is marked by great improvisation "inside" the version, that sort of shimmering Summer 97 "funk" aided by guest percussionist Bob Gullotti, a musician perfect for this "Free" - or any other.
performances.note: Bob Gullotti on a second drum set.

performances.jam: Great -> in from a very solid "Wolfman's Brother." The jam while similar to the post '95 - '96 jam is its own beast; very cool.

-> in from a monster "Stash." The only performance in Fall '97. In addition to an excellent, extended version, the band tacks on a nice 4 1/2 minute ambient jam to the back end of "Free." -> to "Piper."
-> in from "Tweezer." An awesome jam develops that is unique, with great Fishman and Page on the B-3. Unfinished.
Sweet, funky, almost bluesy groove. A great version.
Nice rocking and funky jam that adds a little mustard to the typical "Free" jam.
Trey out in front instead of Mike. Swirling metallic jam that sounds more '99 or '00 than '98. > to "Limb By Limb."
Starts in customary manner, with a lot of bass and nice Trey. A kind of echo-filled groove develops, very mellow.
-> in from a huge "Runaway Jim." Super lazy, summer-style Mike led jam. > to "Meatstick."
Jam starts in typical fashion, but then Trey hits the keyboards for an extended and very different version.
After the initial bass solo, Mike and Fish lay down a really great groove for Trey and Page to play off.

performances.note: Began differently than usual, as the band omitted the usual guitar-driven intro.

performances.jam: -> in from "Ghost." Jam starts in customary manner, but then features an excellent bass and guitar duet/jam.
-> in from an epic "Moma Dance." Sick bass by Mike. Maybe the best straightforward version. Great interplay by Trey and Mike.
> in from a big "Boogie On" -> "Ghost" combo. This one has a really excellent jam.
Some sweet Mike bass, then gets very quiet with just Mike and Trey playing, then Fish and Page jump back in.

performances.jam: Trey pushes through a few early miscues to share in Mike's incendiary groove. Via rhythmic shifts in meter and tone, Trey constructs a mellow, effects-enriched jam, which, colored by Page's wraithlike atmospherics, coasts atop Fish's steady beat, before driving the version to a strong conclusion.

performances.jam: > out of "NMINML". Trey weaves in one of the many "NICU" teases from this show into the first jam, then he suggests minor-key and Page follows him on synths, leading to a lower-boil groove replete with repeating loops and Mike goodness. The band climbs out of the muck and returns to a more upbeat rock jam, with the loops still going, and very neatly returns to "Free" proper.

performances.jam: The usual jam section is perfunctory, but improv continues after the normal ending and soon ascends to a more ethereal plane with thick bass counterpointing magisterial guitar and piano leads. Around 13:00, dirty synth sounds are introduced briefly and then melded into another round of upbeat melodic play which continues through 18:00 when the jam shifts to minor and becomes more rock-oriented, before a final delicate coda > "Esther".
"Free's" second encore and first-ever show-closing appearance comes loaded with heaps of extra synthy spank and filthy wah guitar.
